rtl/pdk/sky130/macro/sky130_sram_4kbyte_.caveat: DEGENERATE - do NOT use for setup signoff. Delay is 99.8x the TT view, of which 80.6x is the temperature factor alone: get_temp_delay_factor (compiler/base/hierarchy_spice.py:637-649) divides by (nom_supply - vthresh) with vthresh extrapolated linearly in temperature, which reaches zero at 100.94 C. This corner sits 0.94 C below that pole, and at 101 C the same model returns a NEGATIVE delay. The resulting min_period 177.497 ns (5.63 MHz, vs 1.779 ns / 562 MHz at TT) is a model artifact, not a slow-corner estimate. Gap G1 stays open. OpenRAM's analytical corner is the TT number multiplied by three algebraic factors (process letter, nom_supply/vdd, and a linearised threshold shift), not an independent derivation: compiler/base/hierarchy_spice.py:610-651. cell_leakage_power is bit-identical to the TT view (0.035146 mW) at every corner - the model does not scale leakage with PVT at all - and max_transition stays at the 0.5 default. Not usable as a power or leakage view.

rtl/pdk/sky130/macro/sky130_sram_4kbyte_.caveat: Numerically plausible but still analytical, so NOT a hold-signoff view. Delay is 0.447x the TT view, which is exactly the product of the three factors (0.9 * 0.923 * 0.539); min_period 0.796 ns. Gap G2 stays open. OpenRAM's analytical corner is the TT number multiplied by three algebraic factors (process letter, nom_supply/vdd, and a linearised threshold shift), not an independent derivation: compiler/base/hierarchy_spice.py:610-651. cell_leakage_power is bit-identical to the TT view (0.035146 mW) at every corner - the model does not scale leakage with PVT at all - and max_transition stays at the 0.5 default. Not usable as a power or leakage view.

pins.views_note: Verilog, LEF, GDS (gzip) and three Liberty views are imported: TT 1.8 V 25 C, SS 1.60 V 100 C and FF 1.95 V -40 C. The slow and fast views were produced on 2026-11-14 by flow/sram/gen_4kb_1rw1r_32x1024_corners.py, which adds use_specified_corners to the pinned config (nominal_corner_only is left True; it is not consulted for the corner list). The same run re-derived the TT view byte-identically, so the corner machinery does not perturb TT. GAPS G1 AND G2 NEVERTHELESS STAY OPEN, and neither new view may be used for signoff (usable_for_signoff: false on both). All three come from OpenRAM's analytical delay model, not SPICE characterization: a corner view is the TT number scaled by three algebraic factors, leakage is bit-identical across all three corners, and the slow corner's 80.6x temperature factor sits 0.94 C below a pole in that factor's formula (negative delays above 100.94 C) - see each view's caveat and flow/sram/records/20261114-gen-4kb-corners/notes.txt. Closing G1 or G2 needs SPICE characterization of the macro, which is out of scope here and has not been done. DRC/LVS were off (magic/netgen not on the worker): the GDS is not signed off here. LEF and GDS are not byte-reproducible across runs (the Verilog and the Liberty are), so the hashes pin these specific files, not the generator output in general.
